questions.question_text: The rate of depression in males is as much as in females in which of the following age groups?
questions.explanation:
In pre-pubescent age group, the prevalence is up to 3% with 1:1 gender ratio. In adolescent age group the prevalence is 8% for males and
14% for females.

questions.question_text: Which mode of treatment is the mainstay in the management of encopresis?
questions.explanation:
In most cases of encoperesis, considerable family discord and distress are common. It is important to reduce the family tensions about the
symptom and a nonpunitive atmosphere is established. Education of the family and correction of misperceptions that a family may have
about soiling must occur before treatment.A paediatric referral is always indicated. Behavioural methods are the mainstay of treatment and
ongoing behavioural intervention to enhance appropriate bowel behaviour and diminish anxiety related to bowel movement.

questions.question_text: What genetic aetiology most increases the risk of the parents having a further child with Down's syndrome?
questions.explanation:
In about 94% of cases, Down syndrome is caused by primary non-disjunction leading to Trisomy 21. The risk of recurrence of this
abnormality is low if maternal age is also relatively low. But if there is Robertsonian translocation (eg 14:21), then risk of recurrence shoots
up.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not routinely recommended in the management of anxiety disorder in children and adolescents?
questions.explanation:
If pharmacological treatment is required, then SSRIs are �rst-line agents. Overall, e�cacy and safety data support the use of selective
serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) to treat childhood social phobia, Separation anxiety disorder and generalised anxiety disorder. Recent
studies have demonstrated the e�cacy of SSRIs for speci�c anxiety disorders. Benzodiazepines are not indicated as a routine treatment in
children due to their potential adverse e�ects. There is also little or no evidence for the e�cacy of other anxiolytics, such as buspirone or
beta-blockers.

questions.question_text: The rate of self-harm in teenagers who identify with Goth culture is around
questions.explanation:
Identi�cation with the Goth youth subculture is strongly associated with self-harm and attempted suicide. A longitudinal cohort study by
Young and colleagues of 1258 people aged 19 who had been followed up since they were 11, found that the prevalence of self-harm and
attempted suicide were 53% and 47% respectively among the participants who identi�ed most strongly with the Goth subculture.
Prevalences of self-harm and attempted suicide in the whole sample were 7% and 6%. Young, R. et al. Prevalence of deliberate self-harm
and attempted suicide within contemporary Goth youth subculture: longitudinal cohort study. BMJ 2006 332: 1058-10

questions.question_text:
In a child with developmental disturbances, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) study revealed hypoplasia of cerebellar vermis. The diagnosis
is most likely to be
questions.explanation:
Hypoplasia of cerebellar vermal lobules VI and VII, in addition to other cortical abnormalities, especially gyri�cation defects, have been
observed in some autistic patients. Other MRI �ndings include increased brain size; increase in the size of the lateral and 4th ventricles;
frontal lobe and cerebellar abnormalities. "The greatest average percentage increase in size occurred in the occipital lobe, parietal lobe, and
temporal lobe. No di�erences were found in the frontal lobes. The increased volume can arise from three di�erent possible mechanisms:
increased neurogenesis, decreased neuronal death, and increased production of nonneuronal brain tissue, such as Glial cells or blood
vessels. Brain enlargement has been suggested as a possible biological marker for autistic disorder". A pathological examination may reveal
abnormal Purkinje cells in cerebellar vermis; abnormal limbic architecture (Excerpt retrieved from Kaplan & Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry
10th ed).

questions.question_text: Gilles de la Tourette syndrome is characterised by all except

options.text: Symptoms present for at least a year
Mean age of onset is seven years

questions.explanation:
Gilles De La Tourette's syndrome is characterised by multiple motor and one or more vocal tics, present for at least a year, causing distress
and impaired function. The onset is before age 18 years. Mean age of onset is 7 years and Male: Female ratio is 3:1.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following genetic disorders is closely associated with autism?
questions.explanation:
Fragile X syndrome, a genetic disorder in which a portion of the X chromosome fractures, appears to be associated with autistic disorder.
Approximately 1-4 percent of children with autistic disorder also have fragile X syndrome. Tuberous sclerosis, a genetic disorder
characterized by multiple benign tumours, with autosomal dominant transmission is also found with greater frequency among children with
autistic disorder. Up to 2 percent of children with autistic disorder may also have tuberous sclerosis. Autistic disorder is also associated with
neurological conditions, notably congenital rubella and phenylketonuria (PKU).

questions.question_text:
In terms of treatments for children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa, which of the following treatments does a large body of evidence
support?
questions.explanation:
Family interventions that directly address the eating disorder are especially useful for children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa. (NICE
Guidelines)

questions.question_text: The male to female ratio for conduct disorder is
questions.explanation:
Estimated rates of conduct disorder among the general population range from 1 to 10 percent, with a general population rate of
approximately 5 percent. The disorder is more common among boys than girls, and the male: female ratio is 4:1 (DSM-IV TR).

questions.question_text: Enuresis is de�ned as voluntary or involuntary voiding of urine usually at night, for a child of age
questions.explanation:
Enuresis is the repeated voiding of urine into a child's clothes or bed; the voiding may be involuntary or intentional. For the diagnosis to be
made, a child must exhibit a developmental or chronological age of at least 5 years.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding childhood elimination disorders?

options.text: Star charts are helpful in encopresis but not in enuresis
Primary enuresis is usually preceded by one year of urinary incontinence
Enuresis occurs more commonly in girls than in boys
Functional encopresis is unrelated to sleep disorders
Enuresis may occur secondary to a psychiatric disorder

correct_answer.text: Enuresis may occur secondary to a psychiatric disorder

questions.explanation:
Enuresis is more common in boys than in girls. Behavioural modi�cation using star charts is the mainstay of treatment for enuresis and
encopresis. The most common co-morbid psychopathology associated with enuresis is depression. Primary enuresis (never dry) and
secondary enuresis (previously dry).

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true with respect to enuresis?

options.text: More common in girls than boys
Cannot be diagnosed without anatomical scan of urinary tract
Cannot occur as a psychiatric complication

questions.explanation:
Enuresis can occur as a psychiatric complication of stressful life events or emotional disturbance; it is not always accompanied by
encopresis. It has high familial association and can be diagnosed without an anatomical scan if history is clearly suggestive. It is 50% more
common in boys than girls.

questions.question_text: Early-onset schizophrenia is associated with all except
questions.explanation:
Early-onset schizophrenia appears to be a more malignant type of schizophrenia, which presents a greater challenge to treat with greater
negative symptoms and cognitive de�cits. It seems to respond less to medication than schizophrenia with adult onset, and the prognosis
may be poorer. Premorbid course EOS cases have increased language, motor, and social delays than adult onset cases. Recent reports have
documented marked neuropsychological de�cits in attention, working memory, and premorbid IQ among children who develop
schizophrenia and its spectrum disorders.

questions.question_text: What is the most likely risk factor that predisposes to criminality at age 17 in a boy who has behavioural problems at the age of 8?
questions.explanation:
Early ADHD is not, on its own, a risk factor for later involvement in crime, but when accompanied by aggressive behaviour, the two together
carry a substantial risk for later persistent o�ending (Mo�tt, 1990). Inadequate parenting at age 8 is a better independent predictor.

questions.question_text: Clinging and di�use non-selectively focused attachment behaviour is seen in
questions.explanation:
Disinhibited attachment disorder of childhood is characterised by a particular pattern of abnormal social functioning that arises during the
�rst 5 years of life. In the early stages, it is usually manifest by clinging and di�use non-selectively focused attachment behaviour. By the age
of 4 years, di�use attachment remains but clinging tends to be replaced by attention seeking and indiscriminately friendly behaviour. During
middle and later childhood this behaviour often persists and depending on circumstances, there may also be associated emotional or
behavioural disturbance.

questions.question_text:
Separation anxiety disorder (SAD) is de�ned as developmentally inappropriate and excessive anxiety concerning separation from home or
from those to whom the individual is attached. This condition occurs in about
questions.explanation:
Di�erent epidemiological studies indicate a prevalence of 3 to 5% in children and adolescents. In contrast to other anxiety disorders, 50 to
75% of children with SAD come from homes of low socioeconomic status. The severity of symptomatology ranges from anticipatory
uneasiness to full-blown anxiety about separation, but children are usually brought to the clinician when SAD results in school refusal or
somatic symptoms. School refusal is reported in about 75% of children with SAD, and SAD is reported to occur in up to 80% of children with
school refusal.

questions.question_text: According to DSM 5 criteria, the core symptoms of ADHD must have their onset
questions.explanation:
Diagnostic criteria: According to DSM-IV criteria, to meet the diagnosis of ADHD, some symptoms must be present before the age of 7 years,
although ADHD is not diagnosed in many children until they are older than 7 years when their behaviours cause problems in school and
other places. In DSM-5, the onset criterion has been changed from "symptoms that caused impairment were present before age 7 years" to
"several inattentive or hyperactive-impulsive symptoms were present prior to age 12". Subtypes have been replaced with presentation
speci�ers that map directly to the prior subtypes. A comorbid diagnosis with autism spectrum disorder is now allowed. The symptom
threshold has been changed for adults with a cuto� for ADHD of �ve symptoms, instead of six required for younger persons, both for
inattention and for hyperactivity and impulsivity.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements about transient tic disorder is incorrect?

options.text: The tics occur many times a day, nearly every day for at least 4 weeks
Quite common in middle childhood, especially among boys.
The tics should last longer than 12 consecutive months
The mean age of onset is between 4-7.
The disturbance is not due to the direct physiological e�ects of a substance (stimulants) or a general medical condition (Huntington's

correct_answer.text: The tics should last longer than 12 consecutive months

questions.explanation:
Diagnostic criteria for Transient tic disorders suggest that the tics occur many times a day, nearly every day for at least 4 weeks, but for no
longer than 12 consecutive months.

questions.question_text: Which of the following positive symptoms is most commonly found in young people with schizophrenia is
questions.explanation:
Delusions are extremely common in schizophrenia, occurring in more than 90% of those who have the disorder. Often, these delusions
involve illogical or bizarre ideas or fantasies. Common schizophrenic delusions include Delusions of persecution, Delusions of reference,
Delusions of grandeur and Delusions of control.

questions.question_text:
A patient who is diagnosed with ADHD is found to have a comorbid bipolar disorder. All of the following symptoms could be explained by
either diagnosis except
questions.explanation:
Decreased need for sleep and lack of sleep is more closely associated with hypomania/mania of bipolar disorder. ADHD on its own does not
produce sleeplessness.

questions.question_text: With respect to the delayed development of empathy skills which of the following is correct?

options.text: Most delayed in hearing children of hearing parents
Most delayed in adopted children of deaf parents
Most delayed in hearing children of hearing parents
Most delayed in deaf children of hearing parents
Most delayed in deaf children of deaf parents

correct_answer.text: Most delayed in deaf children of hearing parents

questions.explanation:
Deaf preadolescents have more di�culty with empathy development than hearing children, and this ability is related to the onset of
deafness (Bachara, 1980). Deaf children born to deaf parents are better in the following areas compared to those born to hearing parents:1.
maturity2. independence3. responsibility taking4. impulse control5. empathizing ability6. better match of parental expectations and
achievements.Bachara, GH. Empathy development in deaf preadolescents. American Annals of the Deaf, 125; 38-41 Feb 1980.Moores, DF
and Meadow-Orlans, KP (ed). Educational and Developmental Aspects of Deafness. Gallaudet University Press 1990. Page 291-93

questions.question_text: The condition commonly associated with autistic spectrum disorders is;
questions.explanation:
Converging �ndings from clinic-based studies (Goldstein and Schwebach 2004) indicate that symptoms consistent with ADHD are present in
a signi�cant proportion of patients with autistic spectrum disorders anywhere between 50-75%. Similarly, symptoms characteristic of autistic
spectrum disorder have been observed in children who meet the criteria for ADHD.

questions.question_text: What is the chance of a 12-year-old boy with conduct disorder developing antisocial personality disorder?
questions.explanation:
Conduct disorder is often chronic and not amenable to treatment. Adult outcomes included antisocial personality disorder, criminality,
substance misuse, and mental disorders. 50% of CD cases have severe persistent antisocial problems as adults.

questions.question_text:
A 12 yr old boy is found to be skipping school repeatedly and using drugs with his friends. He is most likely to have which of the following
diagnosable psychiatric conditions?
questions.explanation:
Conduct disorder is an enduring set of antisocial and aggressive behaviours that evolves over time, usually characterized by aggression and
violation of the rights of others.

questions.question_text:
You are seeing a 2-year-old boy in the clinic, whose vocabulary was limited to only four words (mama, daddy, hi, and more). He rarely
communicated but used these words one at a time in appropriate situations. He supplemented his infrequent verbal communications with
pointing and other simple gestures to request desired objects or actions. What would be the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Communication disorders Communication disorders are among the most common disorders in childhood. Language disorders include
expressive and mixed receptive-expressive language disorder, whereas speech disorders include phonological disorder and stuttering.
Expressive Language disorders Expressive language disorder is diagnosed when a child demonstrates a selective de�cit in expressive
language development relative to receptive language skills and nonverbal intelligence. A child with expressive language disorder is likely to
function below the expected levels of acquired vocabulary, correct tense usage, complex sentence constructions, and word recall. A child
with an expressive language disorder exhibits the following features: limited vocabulary, simple grammar, and variable articulation.
Language understanding (decoding) skills remain relatively intact.

questions.question_text: The risk factors common to children and adolescents who attempt suicide includes all except
questions.explanation: Cognitive distortions characterized by hopelessness and helplessness are often noted in adolescents that attempt suicide.

questions.question_text: The most common co-morbid psychiatric disorder seen in children with ADHD is
questions.explanation:
Co-morbid psychiatric illness is common in ADHD children and is seen in 50-80% of cases. 50% children may meet criteria for 2 comorbid
conditions. Oppositional De�ant disorder in 35-50%, conduct disorder 25%, anxiety disorder 25% and depressive disorder 15%. Learning
disability 15-40%, speci�c language impairment in 15-75% children.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is NOT a core diagnostic feature of ADHD?
questions.explanation:
Clinical features of ADHD: The cardinal features of ADHD are excessive and impairing levels of activity, inattention, and impulsiveness.
Hyperactivity-impulsivity symptoms include �dgeting, moving, getting up and running about, talking excessively; unable to play quietly;
continually interrupting. Inattention symptoms include: easily distracted, poor attention span and cannot sustain attention; poor task
completion; can't organize, and makes mistakes with tasks that require attention; doesn't listen, is forgetful, and loses things for tasks.

questions.question_text: Children with enuresis have shown improvement with which one of the following antidepressant?
questions.explanation:
Classic conditioning with the bell and pad apparatus is generally the most e�ective treatment for enuresis, with dryness resulting in more
than 50 percent of cases. A star chart may be particularly helpful. Imipramine is e�cacious and has been approved for use in treating
childhood enuresis, primarily on a short-term basis. Desmopressin, an antidiuretic compound that is available as an intranasal spray, has
shown some initial success in reducing enuresis.

questions.question_text: What is the common reason for parents and children to seek treatment for Separation anxiety disorder?
questions.explanation:
Children with Separation anxiety disorder (SAD) show anxiety about actual or anticipated separation from or danger to attachment �gure,
sleep disturbances and nightmares, and repeated occurrence of physical symptoms that includes nausea, vomiting, headache, stomach
aches etc especially on occasions that involves separation from a major attachment �gure. The latter may be associated with school refusal
(especially in adolescents)and is the most common reasons for parents and children to seek treatment for SAD.

questions.question_text: In early-onset variant of schizophrenia, the age of onset of symptoms is before
questions.explanation:
Childhood-onset schizophrenia (COS) is a rare and severe form of schizophrenia characterized by an onset of psychotic symptoms by age 12
years, believed to represent a subgroup of a�ected individuals with an increased heritable etiology. The term early-onset schizophrenia is
preferred if the- onset is between ages 12 and 18.

questions.question_text: Heller's syndrome is characterised by normal development until
questions.explanation:
Childhood disintegrative disorder (CDD) also called Heller's syndrome, and disintegrative psychosis is characterized by a marked regression
in several areas of functioning after at least 2 years of apparently normal development. There is normal development for 2-3 years, followed
by a loss of acquired motor, language, and social skills between ages 3 and 4 years.

questions.question_text:
A 15-year-old boy has moderate depression and no suicidality. He is known to be a successful student at his school and has a stable family
support. The most suitable �rst line treatment is
questions.explanation:
CBT alone could be o�ered for this patient with moderate depression - no suicidal risk; refusal of which or failure may prompt use of SSRIs
(in accordance with NICE). There is a certain con�ict of best evidence and recommended practice in adolescent depression. NICE
recommendations are diametrically di�erent from results of TADS study. Treatment of Adolescents with Depression Study (TADS) is the only
published study to compare CBT, �uoxetine, their combination, and placebo. CBT (43% signi�cantly improved) was not superior to placebo
(35%), whereas both combination (71%) including �uoxetine, and �uoxetine alone (61%), were markedly superior to both CBT and to
placebo. The combination treatment (CBT + �uoxetine) showed a faster recovery than any of the other treatments. A possible explanation
for the relatively weak performance of CBT in this study could be the nature of TADS treatment package, which attempted to deliver a large
number of approaches such as problem solving, behaviour activation, cognitive restructuring, emotion regulation, relaxation training etc in a
brief period.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following scales could be used in epidemiological studies as a screening tool for caseness among school-going children before
further diagnostic procedures?
questions.explanation:
CBCL is not a general psychopathology screening tool. "It is used as a device by which parents or other individuals who know the child well
rate a child's problem behaviors and competencies. This instrument can either be self-administered or administered through an interview.
The CBCL can also be used to measure a child's change in behavior over time or following a treatment". The Infant-Toddler Social-Emotional
Assessment (ITSEA) is a parent-completed questionnaire that takes approximately 30 min to complete. "It assesses four broad symptom
domains—externalising, internalising, dysregulation and competence—and generates three indices—maladaptive behaviours, atypical
behaviours and social relatedness. The ITSEA is designed for ages 12-36 months". The Strengths and Di�culties Questionnaire (SDQ) "is a
widely researched 25-item rating scale for youth aged 3-17 years. It addresses emotional symptoms, conduct problems,
hyperactive/inattention, peer relationships and prosocial behaviour. The SDQ also includes functional impact questions to better
discriminate clinical signi�cance".The General Health Questionnaire (GHQ) "is a widely used self-administered questionnaire designed to
screen for mental health problems in adults. The GHQ-36 assesses domains related to anxiety, depression, somatic symptoms and social
dysfunction, and was found to be an e�ective screening tool in a Finnish epidemiological study". The GHQ is recommended for subjects who
are 19 and 21 years of age. SCQ Social communication questionnaire is used the in assessment of autistic spectrum disorders. Connor's
scsle is used in ADHD assessment. (Excerpts retrieved from McClellan et al.,

questions.question_text: The onset of autistic spectrum disorder occurs generally before the age of
questions.explanation:
By de�nition, the onset of the autistic disorder is before the age of 3 years, although, in some cases, it is not recognized until a child is much
older. Autistic disorder is four to �ve times more frequent in boys than in girls

questions.question_text:
Miss. X is a 16-year-old girl who was assessed in the CAMHS outpatient clinic and was diagnosed with Bulimia nervosa? Her mother wishes
her daughter to have a psychotherapeutic intervention. Which one of the following is the most e�ective treatment in this age group?
questions.explanation:
Bulimia nervosa in adolescents is most often treated e�ectively with CBT. CBT is the �rst-line treatment for bulimia nervosa. It has been
found to be the most e�ective treatment in over 35 controlled studies. In these studies the treatment program was usually 16-20 weeks,
after which 40-50% of the patients were abstinent from both bingeing and purging. A reduction of bingeing and purging occurred in 70-95%
of patients. Another 30% of those who did not show improvement immediately after treatment did show improvement to full recovery one
year after treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sleep-related movement disorders is associated with the use of stimulants?
questions.explanation: Bruxism is associated with cocaine, amphetamines, alcohol ingestion and also SSRI use.

questions.question_text: The commonest blood picture expected in adolescents with anorexia nervosa is
questions.explanation: Blood picture in anorexia nervosa: Normocytic normochromic anaemia, Leucopenia and thrombocytopenia

questions.question_text: A report card can be used as a tool in the treatment of which of the following disorders?
questions.explanation:
Behavioral techniques such as learning to attend to a stimulus of interest and ignore disruptive behaviours can help those who su�er from
ADHD. A report card can be used as an e�ective behavioural tool connecting school and home. It can be used as a reinforcer for behaviour.

questions.question_text: In autistic spectrum disorder, the symptom that does not improve over time is
questions.explanation:
Autistic disorder is generally a lifelong disorder with an uncertain prognosis. Overall predictors of good prognosis are early speech
acquisition by ages 5 to 7 years and high intelligence (IQs above 70). Most demonstrated positive changes in communication and social
domains over time. The symptom areas that did not seem to improve over time were those related to ritualistic and repetitive behaviours. In
general, adult-outcome studies indicate that about two-thirds of autistic adults remain severely handicapped and live in complete
dependence or semi dependence, either with their relatives or in long-term institutions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is listed in the ICD-10 criteria for a diagnosis of childhood autism?

options.text: A particular interest in collecting things
Reduced sharing of interests with others

correct_answer.text: Reduced sharing of interests with others

questions.explanation:
Autistic Disorder (historically called early infantile autism, childhood autism, or Kanner's autism) is characterized by symptoms from each of
the following three categories: Qualitative impairment in social interaction, Impairment in communication [language delay is most common
cause for initial referral] and Restricted repetitive and stereotyped patterns of behaviour or interests. By de�nition, the onset of the autistic
disorder is before the age of 3 years, although, in some cases, it is not recognized until a child is much older. Autistic disorder is four to �ve
times more frequent in boys than in girls. There has been an apparent increase in prevalence rates over the years.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms is rare in early-onset schizophrenia?
questions.explanation:
Auditory hallucinations commonly occur in children with schizophrenia. Visual hallucinations are also experienced by a signi�cant number of
children with schizophrenia and often are frightening. Blunted or inappropriate a�ects appear almost universally in children with
schizophrenia. Children with schizophrenia may giggle inappropriately or cry without being able to explain why. Formal thought disorders,
including loosening of associations and thought blocking, are common features among children with schizophrenia. Illogical thinking and
poverty of thought are also often present. A catatonic presentation is uncommon in early onset variants.

questions.question_text: What is the medication of choice for an 8-year-old child with ADHD and tics?
questions.explanation:
Atomoxetine is an NA Reuptake inhibitor showing an e�cacy that parallels methylphenidate. It may be useful where stimulants are abused
or when tics are present; in addition, its once-daily dosing makes it convenient for school-going children.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best-suited treatment option for a teenager with ongoing substance use and ADHD?
questions.explanation:
Atomoxetine has no abuse potential, unlike the amphetamines. Appropriate treatment and response of severe ADHD symptoms can reduce
the later risk of substance abuse.

questions.question_text: Asperger's syndrome is characterised by all except

options.text: Lack of awareness of the feeling of others
Restricted but repetitive stereotyped patterns of behaviour, interests and activities
Impaired intellectual ability and syntactical speech

correct_answer.text: Impaired intellectual ability and syntactical speech

questions.explanation:
Asperger's syndrome is characterised by severe persistent impairment in social interactions, repetitive behaviour patterns, and restricted
interests. IQ and language are normal. Unlike autistic disorder, in Asperger's disorder no signi�cant delays occur in language, cognitive
development, or age-appropriate self-help skills. The clinical features include at least two of the following features of qualitative social
impairment: "Abnormal nonverbal communicative gestures, the failure to develop peer relationships, the lack of social or emotional
reciprocity, and an impaired ability to express pleasure in other persons' happiness. Restricted interests and patterns of behaviour are
always present, but when they are subtle, they may not be immediately identi�ed or singled out as di�erent from those of other children"
(ICD-10). Mild motor clumsiness and a family history of autism may be present.

questions.question_text:
In early childhood, depression will manifest as clingy behaviour, school refusal and exaggerated fears. The percentage of adolescents up to
19 years of age who will have experienced a diagnosable episode of depression in the Europe is
questions.explanation:
Around 20-30% can have a diagnosable episode before age 19, but often these episodes are unattended and appear only in epidemiological
surveys seeking lifetime prevalence

questions.question_text: The most common adverse outcome of conduct disorder seen in adults is the development of which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Approximately 40-50% of children with conduct disorders may develop antisocial personality disorder as adults.

questions.question_text: The common presentations of anxiety disorders in preschool children include
questions.explanation:
Anxiety symptoms vary with age. Tearfulness and clinging in preschool children. Somatic complaints and hypochondriacal fretting are
common in middle childhood (5-12) as are irritability and aggressive behaviour. Separation anxiety disorder and speci�c phobia usually have
onset in early childhood.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders is among the most common psychiatric presentations seen in the adolescents?
questions.explanation:
Anxiety disorders are among the most common conditions a�ecting children and adolescents, with prevalence in the 4% to 20% range. They
adversely impact self-esteem, social relationships, and academic performance.

questions.question_text: Select the adolescent-onset disorder for which social disadvantage is not an established risk factor
questions.explanation:
Anorexia is commoner among upper social class, but social class bias may be modest, and social disadvantage is not a strong determinant
(Kendell 1973)

questions.question_text: In PANDAS, Which of the following psychiatric symptoms is rare?
questions.explanation:
An auditory hallucination is not a feature of PANDAS syndrome. It is an autoimmune syndrome associated with OCD and/or a tic disorder,
with pre-pubertal onset, characterised by episodic exacerbations of symptoms in association with evidence of group A beta haemolytic
streptococcal infection.

questions.question_text: Seizures and irregular respiration are commonly associated features seen in
questions.explanation:
An associated feature of Rett syndrome is irregular respiration, with episodes of hyperventilation, apnoea, and breath holding. The
disorganized breathing occurs in most patients while they are awake; during sleep, the breathing usually normalizes. Many patients with
Rett's disorder also have scoliosis and spasticity. Developmental arrest plateaus and many may reach adulthood although disability is severe
and prognosis poor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has the most supportive evidence base for the treatment of obsessive-compulsive disorder in childhood?
questions.explanation:
Amongst all antidepressants, Sertraline has the most supportive evidence base for the treatment of Obsessive-compulsive disorder (the
Paediatric OCD Treatment Study- POTS)

questions.question_text: The onset of oppositional de�ant disorder is generally between the ages
questions.explanation:
Although the oppositional de�ant disorder can begin as early as 3 years of age, it typically is noted by 8 years of age and usually not later
than adolescence.

questions.question_text: The most important organic cause to be excluded for children with encopresis is
questions.explanation:
Although encopresis is considered a nonorganic disorder, more than three-fourths of children with encopretic behaviour may show
evidence of chronic constipation, leading to infrequent defecation, withholding of bowel movements, which then leads to impaction and
eventual over�ow soiling. However, it is important to exclude organic cause such as Hirschsprung's disease, anorectal pathology,
neurological problems; nutritional disorders and medication-induced.

questions.question_text: The known risk factors for child abuse include all except

options.text: Parent �gure who is biologically unrelated to the child
Parent who was abused as a child

questions.explanation:
Although child abuse occurs at all socioeconomic levels, it is highly associated with poverty and psychosocial stress, especially �nancial
stress. Child maltreatment is strongly correlated with less parental education, underemployment, poor housing, welfare reliance, and single
parenting.

questions.question_text:
Melatonin is considered to be an e�ective treatment for children with learning disabilities and sleep disorders. Which of the following
signi�cantly improves on treatment with this drug?
questions.explanation:
All forms of insomnia are common in children with learning di�culties, autism, ADHD and sensory impairments (particularly visual).
Although behavioural interventions should be the primary intervention and have a robust evidence base, exogenous melatonin is now the
�rst line medication for childhood insomnia. It decreases the time taken to fall asleep (sleep latency). A meta-analytic study by Braam et al.
showed that melatonin treatment decreased sleep latency by a mean of 34 minutes, increased total sleep time by a mean of 50 minutes and
signi�cantly reduced the number of wakes per night. (Ref: The Maudsley prescribing guidelines (pg 279)- 10th edition)

questions.question_text: According to DSM criteria, ADHD is present in what percentage of children?
questions.explanation:
ADHD may a�ect as many as 10% of the population in the United States. Approximately 5% of children ages 9 to 17 are a�ected at any given
time, and a possible 2-4% of adults are a�ected. The occurrence of ADHD is reported worldwide; statistical variations may be due to cultural
perceptions of behavior.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pharmacological options is suitable for the treatment of a girl with ADHD and frequent aggressive outbursts?

questions.question_text: What proportion of 15 to 16-year-old adolescents admit to incidents of deliberate self-harm in the UK?
questions.explanation: Actual incidents of DSH are admitted by only 6.9% of adolescents. The prevalence of ideation is estimated to be far higher.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding enuresis is true?

options.text: Behavioural treatments have no evidence base
Diagnosis can be made only after age 3

questions.explanation:
A familial aggregation is noted for enuresis. Most children tend to remit spontaneously, provided the have a strong psychosocial makeup.
Diagnosis can be only made after age 5. Urine alarm is a useful behavioural treatment. ADH in the form of vasopressin is a useful treatment.
